comparison: Both address identical claims (C2, C32-C46, C111) about NUP reduction in App KI neurons. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with multiple complementary approaches. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 raising critical concerns about time-dependent interpretation being confounded by developmental maturation versus age, requesting removal of temporal claims and additional developmental controls (MAP2, GFAP, Gad65) that were not provided.

Both address identical claims (C47-C48) about LAMIN-B1 levels and nuclear morphology. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as important control data showing NUP loss without gross nuclear envelope disruption. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, acknowledging these as valid control data not challenged by reviewers.

OpenEval R3 addresses C49-C51, C120 about intracellular Aβ increases paralleling NUP reduction. Peer R2 addresses overlapping claims C51, C120-C122. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by immunofluorescence data. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 specifically flagging the temporal correlation statement as problematic due to maturation versus age confounding, recommending removal of claims about parallel changes over time.

Both address identical claims (C52-C54, C117-C118) about DAPT treatment reducing Aβ and restoring NUP coverage. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as establishing causal link between Aβ production and NUP loss. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 acknowledging this as part of 'strong' results demonstrating Aβ's role, though expressing general disappointment about lack of new data.

Both address identical claims (C55-C56, C119) about oligomeric Aβ42 specificity in causing NUP loss. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by experiments showing only oligomeric form produces effect. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 acknowledging this demonstrates 'Abeta drives this process' with oligomer specificity.

Both address identical claims (C57-C60) about conditioned media experiments showing extracellular Aβ uptake causes NUP loss. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by media exchange experiments. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 acknowledging this as evidence that 'Abeta drives this process.'

OpenEval R7 addresses C61-C62 about FRAP showing compromised size-exclusion for small proteins. Peer R6 addresses broader set C61-C74 covering multiple transport defects. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by faster recovery kinetics. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 stating 'nuclear envelope function is altered' and editor noting work supports 'nuclear cytoplasmic transport defects.'

OpenEval R8 addresses C63-C65 about 4xEGFP nuclear accumulation showing compromised size-exclusion for large proteins. Peer R6 addresses broader transport defect claims including these. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by steady-state and FRAP data. Peer review rates overall transport findings SUPPORTED as part of demonstrated nuclear envelope dysfunction.

OpenEval R9 addresses C66-C68, C70 about leaky nuclear retention shown by cycloheximide FRAP experiments. Peer R6 addresses broader transport defects including C70. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by increased cytoplasmic GFP after photobleaching. Peer review rates overall transport findings SUPPORTED as part of altered nuclear envelope function.

OpenEval R11 addresses C72-C74 about dextran permeability showing selective entry of 70 kDa but not 500 kDa dextrans. Peer R6 addresses broader transport defects including these claims. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate controls. Peer review rates overall transport findings SUPPORTED as demonstrating altered nuclear envelope function.

OpenEval R12 addresses C75-C79, C81-C82 about impaired active transport (NLS-4xEGFP import, reduced importin-α1, RanGAP1). Peer R7 addresses overlapping claims C75-C79, C82. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites FRAP and immunofluorescence data establishing mechanistic link. Peer review acknowledges these as part of demonstrated nuclear envelope function alterations.

OpenEval R13 addresses C87-C92 about increased necroptosis vulnerability in App KI neurons. Peer R8 addresses overlapping claims C87-C96 (including phosphorylation markers). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites dose-response experiments with appropriate controls. Peer review acknowledges 'KI cells are more sensitive to TNFalpha-induced necroptosis' as demonstrated.

OpenEval R14 addresses C93-C96 about pMLKL and pRIPK3 increases correlating with necroptosis. Peer R8 addresses broader necroptosis claims including these. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites immunofluorescence showing dose-dependent phosphorylation. Peer review acknowledges increased necroptosis sensitivity as part of overall findings.

OpenEval R15 addresses C98-C103 about differential LMB efficacy between genotypes showing nuclear retention defects. Peer R9 addresses overlapping claims C98-C100, C102-C103. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio measurements validating barrier compromise hypothesis. Peer review acknowledges this as part of mechanistic explanation for altered nuclear envelope function.

Both address identical claims (C105-C109) about GppNHp effects showing differential responses between genotypes consistent with barrier compromise. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites cell death assays and immunofluorescence showing WT-specific reduction in necroptosis. Peer review acknowledges this as part of mechanistic link between NPC dysfunction and necroptosis vulnerability.

OpenEval R17 addresses C4, C110 about NPC dysfunction increasing necroptosis susceptibility. Peer R11 addresses C110. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval bases conclusion on collective necroptosis evidence (C87-C109). Peer review acknowledges this integrative conclusion connecting NPC defects to necroptosis, with editor noting work 'may eventually be useful' and Reviewer 2 calling it 'potentially important.'

Both address identical claims (C29-C31) about no differences in phospho-tau and comparable basal cell viability. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites immunofluorescence and viability assays. Peer review acknowledges these as valid characterization data establishing phenotypes are not due to tau pathology or baseline cell death.

OpenEval R20 addresses C121-C122 about Aβ being necessary and sufficient for NUP loss, citing multiple experimental lines. Peer R2 addresses overlapping claims C51, C120-C122. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by DAPT, oligomer treatment, and media exchange experiments. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN due to temporal interpretation concerns about maturation versus age confounding.

Both address identical claims (C123-C126) about prior work on intracellular Aβ accumulation. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by extensive citations providing important context. Peer review rates UNSUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 'disappointed' that authors failed to adequately contextualize findings with prior nuclear Aβ pathology literature (Pensalfini 2014, Lee 2022), stating discussion 'misrepresents' previous findings and requesting additional experiments on intranuclear amyloid.

OpenEval R28 addresses C130-C131, C71 about aging-related NPC decline. Peer R15 addresses overlapping claims C131, C133-C134. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by citations and age-dependent data. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 requesting retitling discussion section to remove 'age dependence' language due to lack of proper age-matched controls and developmental stage characterization.

OpenEval R29 addresses C132-C133 about normal aging-related Aβ causing NPC decline. Peer R15 addresses overlapping claim C133 plus C131, C134. Both rate UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes causal link is speculative requiring validation. Peer review challenges age-dependence speculation due to lack of requisite developmental controls.

OpenEval R30 addresses C134, C139 about contributions to neuronal loss and disease progression. Peer R15 addresses overlapping claim C134 plus C131, C133. Both rate UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes broader claims require longitudinal studies and in vivo demonstration. Peer review challenges age-dependence framing due to lack of proper controls.

OpenEval finds C69 (nuclear CRTC1 elevation in App KI neurons) SUPPORTED by immunofluorescence data showing compromised protein compartmentalization. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim.

OpenEval finds C39 (RL1/NUP98 colocalization confirming RL1 puncta are NPCs) SUPPORTED by high-resolution confocal imaging with high Pearson's correlation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this validation claim.

OpenEval finds C1, C28 (App KI model characterization and Aβ production) SUPPORTED by citations and authors' immunostaining data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these model characterization claims.

OpenEval finds C3, C70 (NUP loss causes bidirectional transport deficits) SUPPORTED by collective evidence from FRAP, dextran permeability, and CRTC1 studies. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this integrative mechanistic claim.

OpenEval finds C5, C85-C86 (necroptosis mechanism involving nuclear sequestration of phosphorylated proteins) SUPPORTED by citations and validation through LMB/GppNHp experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this mechanistic framework.

OpenEval finds C6, C16, C141 (NPC dysfunction in HD, ALS/FTD, and other neurodegenerative diseases) SUPPORTED by extensive citations, with current study adding AD. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this broader neurodegenerative disease context.

OpenEval rates C7 (NPCs as therapeutic targets) UNCERTAIN, noting claim is speculative as no therapeutic interventions were tested, requiring future validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this therapeutic speculation.

OpenEval finds C112-C116 (NUP functions in transcription, chromatin organization, DNA repair) SUPPORTED by citations providing context for interpreting NUP98/NUP107 loss significance. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this background context.

OpenEval finds C135-C138 (NPC longevity and limited biogenesis in post-mitotic cells) SUPPORTED by extensive citations providing mechanistic context for why NPC damage is consequential in neurons. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this mechanistic background.

OpenEval finds C140 (early disease-stage NPC dysfunction at 2 months) SUPPORTED by data showing NUP reduction and permeability defects despite low plaque burden. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this early-stage timing claim.
